The African armoured gurnard Peristedion cataphractum attains a maximum asymptotic standard length of 40 centimeters [Li = 40 centimeters] according to field-based length-frequency analyses. Specimens approaching this upper size are uncommon in trawl surveys, with most captures consisting of considerably smaller individuals. The standard length at which fifty percent of the population reaches puberty has been estimated at 22 centimeters [Lp = 22 centimeters], a value derived from macroscopic examination of gonadal development across a broad size range of specimens collected from Mediterranean and eastern Atlantic waters. This length at maturity corresponds to a wet weight at puberty of approximately 53 grams [Wwp = approximately 53 grams], calculated from length-weight regressions that describe the species' allometric growth pattern. Individuals exceeding the puberty threshold exhibit well-developed gonads and are considered reproductively competent, though the timing of first spawning is also influenced by seasonal environmental cues.

At hatching, which occurs after an embryonic incubation period of approximately 8 days [ab = approximately 8 days] at a stable ambient temperature of 13.8 °C [T = 13.8 °C], the yolk-sac larva emerges from the chorion at an extremely small size. The wet weight at birth for a newly hatched prolarva is roughly 0.00038 grams [Wwb = roughly 0.00038 grams], a value that is consistent with the modest egg diameter of 0.8 millimeters reported for this species. This lecithotrophic stage relies entirely on endogenous yolk reserves, and the prolarva remains non-feeding until the mouth opens and the yolk is largely absorbed. The duration of this yolk-dependent phase is brief, and the rapid transition to exogenous feeding is critical for larval survival, as mortality rates are typically highest during this early interval when the small body size confers vulnerability to starvation and predation.

At the same stable water temperature of 13.8 °C [T = 13.8 °C], field records and tagging studies indicate that the maximum lifespan documented for Peristedion cataphractum is about 8 years [am = about 8 years]. This comparatively extended lifespan for a fish of its body size suggests a relatively slow pace of life, with individuals investing in somatic growth over multiple seasons before reaching their ultimate body dimensions. The ultimate wet weight attained by fully grown adults has been estimated at 328.6 grams [Wwi = 328.6 grams], a mass that is reached when the fish approaches the asymptotic length of 40 centimeters. Such a body mass places this gurnard among the medium-sized members of its family, with the robust, armoured head and bony scutes contributing substantially to overall weight.

Reproductive output in this species has been characterized by examining females at a standard length of approximately 32 centimeters, which represents a fully mature individual well above the size at puberty. At the typical thermal regime of 13.8 °C [T = 13.8 °C], a female of this size produces an average of 127.2 eggs per spawning event [N_R_i = 127.2 eggs per spawning event], with approximately 1 spawning event per year [F_R_i = approximately 1 spawning event per year]. This annualized fecundity is consistent with the high reproductive output documented in related triglid species such as Trigla lyra. The energetic investment in gamete production is substantial, and females likely invest simultaneously in continued somatic growth and reproductive effort across consecutive spawning seasons.

The prolonged incubation period and the minute size of the yolk-sac larva impose significant constraints on early life history, with the 0.00038 gram [Wwb = 0.00038 gram] neonates being especially vulnerable to all but the smallest planktonic predators. Juveniles grow steadily through the post-settlement phase, and the transition to puberty, marked by a standard length of 22 centimeters [Lp = 22 centimeters] and a corresponding wet weight of 53 grams [Wwp = 53 grams], occurs after a period of several years. The ultimate body size of 40 centimeters [Li = 40 centimeters] standard length and the associated adult mass of 328.6 grams [Wwi = 328.6 grams] are rarely attained before the latter portion of the 8-year maximum lifespan (8 years) [am = 8 years] realized at 13.8 °C [T = 13.8 °C]. Comparative data from congeneric species suggest that this life history strategy, characterized by high fecundity across a moderate longevity window, is typical of demersal triglids occupying continental shelf habitats.
